subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Hadith on Brushing Teeth
overview: Clean teeth are part of the sunnah, not only a health rule. In this sub-strand you will read the Hadith on brushing the teeth, learn why the Prophet (S.A.W.) loved the siwak, and practise brushing as an act of ibadah that pleases Allah.

lessons.title: The Hadith on brushing the teeth
objectives: Read the selected Hadith on brushing teeth.
Explain its meaning in simple words.
lessons.intro: Before standing for swalah, a Muslim prepares more than the prayer mat. The mouth that will recite Al-Fatiha should be clean. The Prophet (S.A.W.) loved this cleanliness and spoke about it in a short Hadith.
lessons.notes:
### The selected Hadith
The Prophet (S.A.W.) said: “Brushing of teeth is a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.” This Hadith is narrated by Ibn Majah. Two results are named. The first is for the mouth: it becomes pure and clean. The second is for Allah: the act pleases Him when it is done as obedience.

### Siwak and the toothbrush
The Prophet (S.A.W.) used a siwak, also called a miswak. It is a small stick, traditionally from the arak tree, used to clean the teeth. A toothbrush and clean toothpaste do the same job of cleaning the mouth when a siwak is not at hand. The aim in the Hadith is a clean mouth, done to please Allah. Using either tool with that intention follows the teaching.

### Another word from the Prophet
He also said that if he had not found it difficult for his community, he would have ordered them to use the siwak for every swalah (Bukhari and Muslim). He did not make it a must before every prayer, because he did not want to place a hardship on people. He still showed how strongly he loved it. Learners should therefore brush regularly and, when they can, clean the teeth before swalah.

Read the selected Hadith until you can say it without the book. Write it in your notebook and remember the narrator, Ibn Majah. The next lesson will ask why this small act matters so much.

keyWords.meaning: a small cleaning stick used on the teeth, following the sunnah
worship, or a good act done to please Allah

examples.problem: A learner says, “Siwak is only an old custom, so brushing has no reward.” What do the two parts of the Hadith reply?
steps: The Hadith says brushing purifies the mouth.
It also says the act is pleasing to Allah.
A toothbrush used for Allah’s pleasure follows the same aim.
examples.answer: Brushing cleans the mouth and pleases Allah. It is not an empty custom.

activity.title: Read the Hadith clearly
steps: Read together: “Brushing of teeth is a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.”
Each learner reads it to a partner and names the narrator, Ibn Majah.
Underline the two results: a clean mouth, and the pleasure of Allah.
Write the Hadith and the meaning of siwak in your notebook.

practice.question: Write the selected Hadith on brushing teeth.
practice.answer: “Brushing of teeth is a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.”

practice.question: Who narrated this Hadith in the Grade 4 design?
What is a siwak?
practice.answer: A small stick, traditionally from the arak tree, used to clean the teeth.

practice.question: Why did the Prophet (S.A.W.) not order siwak before every single swalah?
practice.answer: He did not want to place a hardship on his community, although he loved the practice.

summary: Brushing purifies the mouth and pleases Allah.
The Hadith is narrated by Ibn Majah.
Siwak is the sunnah stick; a toothbrush can also clean the mouth for Allah.

lessons.title: Why brushing the teeth matters
objectives: Give reasons for brushing the teeth regularly.
Name times when a Muslim should brush.
Connect clean teeth with reward from Allah.
lessons.intro: A mouth that is not cleaned develops a bad smell, and teeth that are never brushed begin to ache. Islam joins that health need with worship, so brushing is both hygiene and a way to earn reward.
lessons.notes:
### Reasons that join health and faith
Brushing matters for several reasons that belong together:

- It purifies the mouth, which is the wording of the Hadith.
- It pleases Allah, so it is an act of ibadah when the intention is right.
- It removes bits of food and the smell that embarrasses a person standing near others in swalah.
- It protects the teeth from decay and the gums from disease. A painful tooth can even distract a person from reciting well.
- It follows the Prophet (S.A.W.), who loved the siwak.
- The Muslim who brushes seeking Allah’s pleasure hopes for reward, not only for a bright smile.

### When to brush
Brush when you wake up, before you sleep, and whenever the mouth smells or feels unclean. Clean the teeth before swalah when you can, and before reading the Qur’an, so the mouth that praises Allah is fresh. Do not wait for a toothache. A sunnah that is kept every day is easier than a treatment later.

### Assessing the importance
Some learners brush only on the morning of a school photo. That misses the Hadith. The Prophet (S.A.W.) connected brushing with purification and with Allah’s pleasure, so it belongs to ordinary days, not only to special ones. A Muslim values the act because Allah rewards obedience, and because the Prophet made it part of a clean life.

keyWords.meaning: keeping the mouth and teeth clean
the good that Allah gives for an act done to please Him

examples.problem: Yusuf brushes only when visitors are coming. Use the Hadith to assess this habit.
steps: The Hadith gives two aims: a pure mouth and Allah’s pleasure.
Both aims apply every day, not only when guests arrive.
He should also brush on waking, before sleep and before swalah when he can.
examples.answer: The habit is too rare. Brushing is a daily sunnah for cleanliness and for Allah’s pleasure.

activity.title: Discuss why we brush
steps: In small groups, discuss the question: Why do you brush your teeth?
Sort your reasons into two columns: health of the mouth, and pleasing Allah.
Add the times of day when a Muslim should brush.
Present the chart and write the agreed points in your notebook. Respect every serious answer.

practice.question: Give three reasons why brushing the teeth is important.
practice.answer: Any three: it purifies the mouth, it pleases Allah, it prevents bad smell and tooth decay, it follows the Prophet, and it can earn reward.

practice.question: Name three times when a learner should brush.
practice.answer: Any three: after waking, before sleeping, before swalah, before reading the Qur’an, or when the mouth is unclean.

practice.question: When does brushing become an act that earns reward?
practice.answer: When it is done with the intention of following the Prophet (S.A.W.) and pleasing Allah.

summary: Brushing cleans the mouth, protects the teeth and pleases Allah.
Good times include waking, sleeping, and before swalah when possible.
The reward comes when the intention is to obey Allah.

lessons.title: Brushing the teeth as ibadah
objectives: Demonstrate a correct way to brush the teeth.
Make the right intention before brushing.
Recite a short class poem that reminds the group of the Hadith.
lessons.intro: Holding a brush the right way, reaching every side of the teeth, and beginning with an intention turns a bathroom habit into worship. This lesson practises that skill.
lessons.notes:
### Intention first
Before you brush, set the intention in your heart: “I am cleaning my teeth to purify my mouth and to please Allah, following the Prophet (S.A.W.).” You do not have to say a long sentence aloud. The intention makes the same movements into ibadah. Without it, the teeth may still become clean, but the worship in the Hadith is missed.

### How to brush
Use a siwak or a soft toothbrush.

- Brush the outer sides of the upper and lower teeth.
- Brush the inner sides.
- Brush the chewing surfaces.
- Clean the tongue gently so that smell does not remain.
- Do not swallow toothpaste. Spit it out and rinse with clean water.
- Do not share a siwak or a toothbrush with another person.
- Brush gently. Scrubbing very hard can hurt the gums.

If you use a siwak, rinse it before and after use and keep it in a clean place. If you use a brush, replace it when the bristles are worn out.

### A class poem to remember
You can learn lines like these and clap a simple rhythm. They are a class reminder, not a verse of the Qur’an:

Brush the teeth, purify the mouth,
Please your Lord at dawn and night.
Siwak or brush, the aim is one,
A clean mouth for the One we praise.

Practise every morning and night this week. That regular practice is how a learner appreciates the Hadith and hopes for reward from Allah (S.W.T.).

keyWords.meaning: a poem or song, here a class poem about the sunnah of brushing

examples.problem: Asha brushes quickly across only the front teeth and swallows the toothpaste. What should she change?
steps: She should brush outer, inner and chewing surfaces, and the tongue.
She should spit out the toothpaste and rinse.
She should intend the act for Allah.
examples.answer: Brush all the surfaces gently, clean the tongue, spit and rinse, and make the intention to please Allah.

activity.title: Demonstrate brushing and share a poem
materials: A toothbrush or a clean siwak for demonstration
steps: Your teacher demonstrates brushing the outer, inner and chewing surfaces, then the tongue, and rinsing.
Each learner demonstrates the same actions, using a finger if a personal brush is not available, without sharing brushes.
In groups, recite or sing a short poem or qasida on brushing the teeth. You may use the class lines or write two new lines.
Write the steps and your intention in your notebook.

practice.question: What intention can a Muslim make before brushing?
practice.answer: To purify the mouth and please Allah, following the Prophet (S.A.W.).

practice.question: Name the surfaces of the teeth that should be brushed.
practice.answer: The outer sides, the inner sides and the chewing surfaces. The tongue should be cleaned as well.

practice.question: Why should toothpaste not be swallowed?
practice.answer: It is for cleaning and should be spat out, then the mouth rinsed with clean water.

practice.question: How does regular brushing show appreciation of the Hadith?
practice.answer: The learner keeps the sunnah in order to please Allah and hopes for reward, not only for appearance.

summary: Begin brushing with the intention to please Allah.
Clean all tooth surfaces and the tongue, then rinse.
A class poem can help the group remember the Hadith.

quiz.question: What does the Hadith narrated by Ibn Majah say about brushing the teeth?
options: It purifies the mouth and pleases Allah
quiz.explanation: The Hadith calls brushing a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.

quiz.question: What is a siwak?
options: A stick used to clean the teeth
quiz.explanation: The Prophet (S.A.W.) used a siwak, traditionally from the arak tree.

quiz.question: Why did the Prophet (S.A.W.) not make siwak a command before every swalah?
options: He did not want to burden his community
quiz.explanation: He would have ordered it for every prayer had it not been a hardship. He still loved it.

quiz.question: Which of these is a sound reason to brush?
options: Only so that a photo looks good
To purify the mouth and please Allah
quiz.explanation: Health and Allah’s pleasure belong together in this Hadith.

quiz.question: When is a good time to brush?
options: Only after a toothache has lasted a week
quiz.explanation: Regular times include waking, sleeping, and before swalah when possible.

quiz.question: Brushing earns reward when the person…
quiz.answer: Intends to follow the Prophet (S.A.W.) and to please Allah.
quiz.explanation: The same movements without that intention are hygiene, but the ibadah is in the intention.

quiz.question: Which surfaces should be brushed?
options: Only the teeth that already hurt
quiz.explanation: All those surfaces, and the tongue, need cleaning.

quiz.question: What should you do with toothpaste?
options: Leave it on the teeth all day
quiz.explanation: Toothpaste is not food. Spit it out and rinse with clean water.

quiz.question: Sharing a toothbrush with a friend is…
options: unwise, because each person should use a clean personal brush or siwak
quiz.explanation: Each learner keeps his or her own clean siwak or brush.

quiz.question: Which action shows that a learner values this Hadith?
options: Hiding the brush and never using it
Mocking a classmate who uses a siwak
quiz.explanation: Appreciation is shown by regular practice done to please Allah.
